summary: Describes the RFC Editor model that divides RFC Series responsibilities among the RFC Series Editor, the RFC Production Center, and the RFC Publisher. It covers IAB oversight through the RSOC and the relationship with the IETF LLC. It was replaced by RFC 9280.

eli5.summary: This explains who does which job in producing RFCs, like roles in a newspaper. It was later replaced by RFC 9280.

questions: what is the rfc production center
subtitle: How the RFC Editor is organized into specialized roles and oversight.

tldr.problem: The RFC Editor function had grown too complex for a single person or simple organizational structure, requiring clearer roles, stronger oversight, and better coordination with the IETF's administrative structure.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8728 divides RFC Editor responsibilities into three functions (RFC Series Editor, RFC Production Center, and RFC Publisher), adds oversight through the RSOC (RFC Series Oversight Committee), and aligns the structure with the IETF LLC.
tldr.outcome: This provided a sustainable organizational model with clear responsibilities, accountability through IAB oversight, and the ability to hire contractors for production and publishing while keeping editorial leadership in-house.

today: RFC 8728 was declared obsolete in 2024 when RFC 9280 was issued as the updated RFC Editor model specification, reflecting further evolution of the roles and structure.

sections.title: RFC Editor as an Organization
sections.content:
RFC 8728 describes the organizational model for the RFC Editor, the function responsible for publishing the RFC Series. The RFC Series has grown to over 9,000 documents since 1969, and the task of editing, producing, and publishing them can no longer be done by a single person. This document divides the RFC Editor function into three separate roles and defines oversight through the Internet Architecture Board.

The RFC itself notes that this is Version 2 of the model, replacing RFC 6635. It aligns the RFC Editor structure with the IETF LLC, which is the administrative corporation that manages IETF operations. The model was designed based on experience running Version 1, feedback from the community, and the new IASA 2.0 (IETF Administrative Support Activity 2.0) structure.
sections.eli5: Like a newspaper, the RFC Editor needs different people: one to run the publication, one to edit and format stories, and one to print and distribute them. The boss of all three reports to a committee that checks their work.

sections.title: The Three Components
sections.content:
RFC 8728 divides RFC Editor responsibilities into three components. The RFC Series Editor (RSE) is the leadership role, responsible for the overall quality, continuity, and evolution of the RFC Series. The RFC Production Center is a contractor who edits documents to comply with RFC style, coordinates with authors and working groups, assigns RFC numbers, and ensures documents are ready for publication. The RFC Publisher is another contractor who announces RFCs on-line, provides access to them, manages the RFC errata system, stores and preserves records, and provides backups.

The RSE manages and provides strategic direction to the Production Center and Publisher, but does not do day-to-day operational management of them. The RFC Production Center and Publisher are selected through a competitive Request for Proposal process overseen by the IETF LLC, and the RSE participates in evaluating proposals.
sections.eli5: The Editor-in-Chief (RSE) decides what to publish and sets policy. The Production team edits and numbers the documents. The Publisher team prints, archives, and shares them with readers.

sections.title: The RFC Series Editor
sections.content:
The RFC Series Editor is appointed by the Internet Architecture Board (IAB) and formally hired by the IETF LLC. The RSE is a senior technology professional who provides strategic leadership and represents the RFC Series inside and outside the IETF.

RSE responsibilities include managing the RFC Production Center and Publisher contractors, ensuring the RFC Series evolves to meet community needs, designing improvements to production and publication processes, representing the RFC Series to external parties, and working with community members to develop policy consensus. The RFC Editor website is the RSE's responsibility, as is developing consensus versions of vision and policy documents that are then reviewed and approved by the RFC Series Oversight Committee.

The position is expected to require about 20 hours per week on average, with more during IETF meetings and special projects. The RFC 8728 document lists 11 desired qualifications for the RSE, including strategic management experience, communication skills, editorial background, understanding of the IETF process, and experience as an RFC author.
sections.eli5: The Editor-in-Chief decides what the RFC Series should become, talks to readers and writers about it, and makes sure everything works smoothly. The job needs a senior person who understands both writing and organizations.

sections.title: Production and Publishing Contractors
sections.content:
The RFC Production Center contractor edits documents to comply with RFC style rules, records what changes were made, identifies where editorial changes might affect technical meaning and seeks clarification, manages dialogue with authors and working groups, assigns RFC numbers, ensures documents are ready for publication, and coordinates with IANA (Internet Assigned Numbers Authority) to document protocol registry assignments.

The RFC Publisher contractor runs the on-line systems where RFCs are announced and accessed, manages the RFC errata (error reports) system, maintains backups, preserves records of edits and author interactions, authenticates RFCs for legal proceedings, and stores documents for long-term preservation.

Both contractors are selected through an IETF LLC Request for Proposal process. The RSE develops the work scope and participates in vendor selection, but the IETF LLC has final authority over contracting and budget. The RFC Publisher can optionally be the IETF Secretariat itself, rather than an external contractor, at the Selection Committee's choice.
sections.eli5: Production contractors mark up the text and check facts. Publisher contractors run the website, manage corrections, and make sure nothing gets lost.

sections.title: Oversight and Governance
sections.content:
The IAB maintains overall responsibility for the RFC Series and has established the RFC Series Oversight Committee (RSOC) to provide continuous oversight. The RSOC is composed of Internet community experts designated by the IAB, including some IAB members and outside experts with relevant knowledge (general Internet expertise, IETF expertise, publication expertise, and stream expertise). The RSOC approves consensus policy and vision documents developed by the RSE, performs annual reviews of the RSE, and manages the selection process for new RSE candidates.

The IETF LLC, which handles administrative and contractual matters, maintains a separate relationship to the RFC Editor. Figure 2 in the RFC shows the authority structure: the IAB provides oversight of the RSE through the RSOC (shown as a solid line), while the IETF LLC provides contract and budget oversight of the RFC Production Center and Publisher (shown as a dotted line).

When disagreements arise between the RSE, Production Center, Publisher, or document streams, the RFC establishes a process for resolution starting with informal discussion, then RSE decision if necessary, and if needed, formal review by the RSOC and IAB. The RSE can make unilateral decisions to ensure smooth operation, but only while the RSOC evaluates whether policies need adjustment.
sections.eli5: The IAB's committee (RSOC) checks on the Editor-in-Chief every year. The business side (IETF LLC) manages money and contracts. When there is a fight, they try to talk it out, then the Editor decides, then the committee can review.
